correctness.rationale: The exact quadratic for a and b reduces inclusion of every point on the candidate ellipsoid boundary to ha sqrt(d)(|q|-1/sqrt(d))^2>=0. The full 4(d-1)-point transformed contact system with weight d/[4(d-1)] satisfies both John moment equations exactly, so the ellipsoid is globally optimal and unique. The two high-dimensional asymptotics follow from direct Taylor expansion and monotone comparison; 28,307 standalone numerical checks complement, not replace, these proofs.

originality.rationale: John 1948 is a universal characterization, not this explicit application. Full material comparisons with Güler–Gürtuna 2007 Sections 3, 5–7 show optimization of *ellipsoidal slabs* rather than intersections of two balls. Finch 2013 §1 computes volume, area, and mean width of the same lens, but no John axes. Paouris–Pivovarov 2015 studies stochastic intrinsic-volume inequalities for intersections of balls. Searches for the exact lens ellipsoid and its high-dimensional crossover did not disclose coverage. Historical-priority uncertainty remains; absence of hits is not itself a novelty certificate.
residual_risks: An equivalent explicit John ellipse/ellipsoid computation may exist in older or nondigitized specialist references on spherical lenses or affine approximations.

value.rationale: The exact unique ellipsoid and its 4(d-1)-point contact certificate solve a natural affine approximation problem for spherical lenses. The full asymptotic trichotomy identifies a sharp transition at center half-separation order 1/sqrt(d) and quantifies fixed-gap exponential collapse, a dimension-driven phenomenon not supplied by classical lens intrinsic volumes. This is a structurally motivated benchmark in convex geometry rather than an arbitrary parameter evaluation.
